headline: South Maui plan review focuses on flooding and water policies

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.voteItem: Amend policy 2.3.3 to the recommended language
meeting.summary: The committee reviewed South Maui Community Plan policies, saw drone images of flooded gulches, and passed amendments on water use and injection wells.
meeting.recap: Members began reviewing plan Sections 2.3 and 2.4.[[0:07:07]] He said flood water and mud reached every condo at Sugar Beach.[[0:12:36]] One testifier asked for 150-foot buffers around gulches.[[0:54:10]] Another testifier urged the county to stop building in flood zones and wetlands.[[1:03:15]] Members voted 8–0 to meet in executive session (a closed-door meeting) to consult their lawyers.[[1:50:30]] Members voted 7–0 to add a county department to the consultation list in policy 2.3.10.[[2:53:41]] Members voted 6–0 to require gray or recycled water in county parks and gardens when available and legally permissible.[[3:47:44]] Members voted 6–0 to move toward ending wastewater injection wells in South Maui.[[4:00:32]]
decided: The amendment passed 7–0, with two members excused.
The committee voted 8–0 to go into executive session to consult with legal counsel.
The committee voted 7–0 to use the recommended wording, which adds a county department to the consultation list.
The committee voted 7–0 to delete the policy because it nearly matches action 3.14.
The motion passed with six ayes; the captions garble the "no" count.
The committee voted 6–0 to support catchment and gray water where allowed by the State Department of Health.
A motion was moved and seconded, but the captions do not record a vote.
The committee voted 6–0 to move toward eliminating wastewater injection wells in South Maui.
meeting.next: A deputy corporation counsel may draft policy language on pre-authorization during emergencies. The chair suggested a member could propose a goal 2.5 policy on moving natural resources out of a moku with consultation.

moments.q: Debate on consulting before moving sand, pōhaku and sediment
"we can't eliminate injection wells at the time because we need 100% backup"
